name: Kentucky
summary: Statutes: apps.legislature.ky.gov serves each KRS section as a PDF at statute.aspx?id=N, where the numeric id comes from the chapter page (title page, then chapter, then section); fetch_doc.py reads them, built URLs are gated for WebFetch, and Justia 2025 is a constructible tier-2 fallback. The constitution and session laws (Ky. Acts) are on the same host, and KAR regulation pages have constructible URLs (3-digit padded) with engrossed PDFs; the Administrative Register is published as monthly PDFs. Consolidated court rules (CR, RCr, KRE, RAP, SCR) are only on govt.westlaw.com, which is blocked; kycourts.gov serves only the Supreme Court's adopting and amending orders as PDFs (RAP order 2022-49 is a corpus candidate). Case law: the official opinion hosts fail (opinions.kycourts.net has a TLS error; appellatepublic.kycourts.net is a JavaScript app). Supreme Court and Court of Appeals minutes PDFs on apps.kycourts.net list every opinion and discretionary-review order by docket. Justia supplies the opinion text, with cases.justia.com slip PDFs readable by the script.

citation_map.notes: KRS sections are chapter.section (413.140, 342.0011, 422A.0702) and the insurance code uses chapter.article-section (304.20-450); chapters can carry a letter suffix (15A, 164A, 422A). 'KRS 311.530 to 311.620' or '311.530-311.620' is a range: the regex takes the first section, and the -NNN tail only binds to 2-4 digit article-section forms after a dot. KRS URLs are not constructible: statute.aspx?id= is an opaque id read from the chapter page. KRE are numbered rules (KRE 702); KRS chapter 422A holds only 'Renumbered as KRE nnn' stubs, so KRE text is not on the legislature site. Kentucky court rules carry no state marker in practice ('CR 12.02(f)', 'RCr 11.42', 'KRE 702', 'SCR 3.130(1.7)', 'RAP 41'). The dotted CR NN.NN, RCr, KRE and SCR d.ddd forms are treated as distinctive. Bare 'RAP 41' is shared with Washington's RAP and bare 'CR 56' with Washington's CR, so both are context_required. SCR is matched only in the d.ddd form, which keeps Wisconsin 'SCR 20:1.7' and other states' SCR forms out. Kentucky style is '(Ky. App. 2021)'; Bluebook is '(Ky. Ct. App. 2021)'. Before 1976 the Court of Appeals was the highest court, so cite '(Ky. 1970)'. No public-domain citation. Dockets: YYYY-SC-NNNNNN-XX and YYYY-CA-NNNNNN-XX, with type suffixes MR (matter of right), DG/DGE (discretionary review granted), WC (workers' comp), ME, OA (original action), KB (bar), TG (transfer granted). The suffix list keeps Mississippi '-COA/-SCT' and Florida trial '-CA-...-O' numbers out. Unpublished opinions are cited under RAP 41 (formerly CR 76.28(4)(c)); they must be attached to the brief and usually carry a WL cite. 'disc. rev. denied' is Kentucky's subsequent-history phrase, but North Carolina uses 'disc. review denied', so the bare form is context_required. CourtListener ids are from memory and unverified.

sources.title: Kentucky Revised Statutes (KRS) online
sources.official_status_evidence: KRS page notice: the statutes on the site are 'an unofficial posting' and 'do not constitute official text'; the certified versions are to be consulted (https://legislature.ky.gov/Law/Statutes/Pages/default.aspx). The Certified Versions page says that under KRS 7.138(2) only the official LRC database or a certified print version (LexisNexis, Thomson Reuters) may be cited in court (https://legislature.ky.gov/Law/Statutes/Pages/KRSEDS.aspx). The same page bars commercial use without agreement (KRS 61.874).
sources.coverage: All KRS chapters, current text with history notes and LRC notes; repealed and renumbered sections remain as one-line stubs.

access.navigation: KRS title page (lists every chapter, 'CHAPTER 413 LIMITATION OF ACTIONS') -> chapter.aspx?id={opaque chapter id} (lists sections as '.140 Actions to be brought within one year.') -> statute.aspx?id={opaque section id}, which returns the section as a PDF. Ids are not derivable from the citation: always read them from the chapter page (fetch_doc.py links <chapter url> '^\.140 ' --regex). The title page shows chapter numbers and names only; chapter pages show every section number.

automation.notes: WebFetch on a built statute.aspx URL and on the title page returned PROVENANCE_REQUIRED (not retried); WebFetch read statute.aspx?id=50197 (a search-result URL) correctly, so it handles the PDFs when the URL has provenance. Use fetch_doc.py. Sections are short PDFs (KRS 413.140: 2 pages; 342.0011: 8 pages).

currency.where: title page and chapter pages, under the heading; chapter pages also show the database update date
currency.observed: Includes enactments through the 2026 Regular Session; KRS database was last updated on 10/17/2026

hazards: unofficial online text: KRS 7.138(2) requires the official or certified version for citation in court

chapter-page link text is '.140 Title', without the chapter number: filter on '^\.140 '
renumbered and repealed sections return a one-line PDF stub ('422A.0702 Renumbered as KRE 702.')
history and LRC notes follow the text in the same PDF: stop quoting at 'Effective:' / 'History:'

sources.title: Kentucky Administrative Regulations (KAR)
sources.official_status_evidence: KAR home: 'Unofficial WWW Version'; the regulations are 'an unofficial posting' of the LRC's official internal database (https://legislature.ky.gov/Law/kar/Pages/default.aspx).

access.pattern_rules: Zero-pad title, chapter and regulation to 3 digits: 201 KAR 9:260 -> titles/201/009/260/; 13 KAR 2:020 -> titles/013/002/020/ (titles/13/... is 404). The page links 'Download PDF' -> /law/kar/downloads/docs/{opaque doc id}/document.engrossed.pdf (read that link from the page). Emergency regulations (E suffix) are not at .../005E/ (404): use the chapter page or EmergencyRegs.aspx.

automation.notes: WebFetch read a KAR engrossed PDF from a search result; built regulation URLs are expected to be gated, as on the KRS pages. HTML pages are long (401 KAR 5:005: 164,689 chars) because the text appears twice: prefer the engrossed PDF.
